title: For 38 years, this man lived beside a miracle he could never reach.
paragraphs: For 38 years, this man lived beside a miracle he could never reach.
Think about that for a moment.

Thirty-eight years of watching other people step into the water.
Thirty-eight years of hoping the next moment would be his turn.
Thirty-eight years of disappointment.
Day after day he lay beside the Pool of Bethesda — surrounded by people who were sick, desperate, and waiting for something supernatural to happen.
Everyone believed that when the water stirred, healing would come.

So the sick gathered there.
The weak gathered there.
The broken gathered there.
And this man waited.

But every time the water moved…
someone else got there first.
Year after year he watched others receive what he had been praying for.
Can you imagine the emotional weight of that?

Watching miracles happen for everyone else…
while your situation never changes.

Watching hope rise…
and fall again.

Watching opportunity come close…
but never close enough.
After 38 years, disappointment becomes familiar.
After 38 years, waiting becomes normal.
After 38 years, people stop expecting change.
Then one day something different happened.
Jesus walked into that place.

Out of all the sick people lying around the pool…
Jesus walked straight to the man who had been there the longest.
And He asked a question that seems almost strange.
"Do you want to be made well?" (John 5:6)
At first, that question sounds obvious.
Of course he wants to be healed.
But look carefully at the man's answer.
He didn’t say yes.
Instead, he explained why it couldn’t happen.
"Sir, I have no one to help me into the pool when the water is stirred. While I am trying to get in, someone else goes down ahead of me."
Do you see what happened?
Jesus asked about desire.
The man answered with reasons.
Jesus asked about possibility.
The man explained his limitations.
After 38 years, the problem had become his identity.
The system had become his explanation.
The waiting had become his story.
And this is where the lesson gets powerful.
Sometimes we are not stuck because God is silent.
Sometimes we are stuck because we have learned to live inside the story of why things cannot change.
We explain our situation.
We defend our limitations.
We repeat the same reasons over and over again.
But Jesus did something unexpected.
He didn’t stir the water.
He didn’t fix the system.
He didn’t move the crowd.
He simply gave a command.
"Rise. Take up your mat and walk." (John 5:8)
And instantly, the man who had been waiting 38 years stood up.

Thirty-eight years of waiting…
ended with one word from Jesus.
That is the moment that changes everything.
Because the miracle was never really about the pool.
The pool was just the place people gathered.
The power was never in the water.
The power was always in Jesus.
Sometimes we spend years waiting for the right moment…

Waiting for the right opportunity.
Waiting for the right connection.
Waiting for the right conditions.
But the truth is this:
Your breakthrough does not come when circumstances change.
Your breakthrough comes when Jesus speaks into your life.
The man thought the answer was in the water.
But the answer was standing right in front of him.
And here is a powerful thought:

You can sit beside opportunity for years
while believing the wrong story about your life.

You can live near miracles
and still believe you are the exception.

You can become so familiar with your struggle
that you stop imagining life beyond it.
But Jesus interrupts those stories.
He walks into places where people have given up.
He speaks into situations that seem permanent.
He tells people who have been stuck for decades:
"Rise."
Not next year.
Not when conditions improve.
Not when someone helps you.
Now.
That is the authority of Jesus.
And that is why this story still speaks to us today.
Because many of us are sitting beside our own "pools."
Waiting.
Watching.
Hoping something changes.
But maybe the real question Jesus is asking is the same one He asked that man:
"Do you want to be made well?"
Not just healed physically.
But healed emotionally.
Healed spiritually.
Healed from the story that says your life cannot change.
Because when Jesus speaks, the impossible can move in a single moment.
Thirty-eight years can end in one command.
One encounter can change everything.
One word from Jesus can lift you off the mat you have been lying on for years.
And the mat you once carried as a burden…
Becomes the testimony you carry in your hands.
Now I’m curious:
What do you think kept the man waiting for 38 years?

Was it his condition…
or the mindset he developed while living with it?
